title: temporary-pin-override-playbook
body:
Purpose and scope:

This is an operator-facing playbook describing when and how to perform a TEMPORARY region pin 'override' for customer workloads. It is intentionally narrow: this document does NOT change long-term regional policy or legal decisions. It covers authorization, telemetry, rollback, audit evidence, and communication templates for short-lived exceptions (TTL up to 96 hours).

Why this exists (quick summary):
- Customers occasionally need short, urgent exceptions to region pins (e.g., catastrophic regional outage, capacity exhaustion, or legal emergency where data must be processed elsewhere temporarily).
- Ad-hoc adoptions without controls have caused silent data locality drift in past drills. This playbook standardizes approvals, telemetry, and rollback so overrides remain auditable and reversible.

Key definitions:
- Region pin: the tenant-level enforcement that routes and stores customer data in the specified geo (EU, US, APAC, etc.).
- Temporary override: operator-triggered, time-bound bypass of region pin to route to a fallback region or alternate capacity tier. Always annotated and auditable. TTL <= 96 hours required.
- Emergency vs. Operational override: Emergency = safety/compliance incident (legal hold, law enforcement). Operational = capacity/latency outage or maintenance. Authorization differs.

Authorization matrix (who can approve):
- Emergency override: Required approvers = 1 Engineering On-call lead (SRE/Platform), 1 Legal on-call, 1 Product owner. Escalation: CEO or Head of Security if Legal unavailable.
- Operational override: Required approvers = 1 SRE/Platform lead OR 1 Product owner; notify Security.
- Fast-track (major outage <30 minutes): SRE lead can initiate with post-hoc legal acknowledgement within 4 hours.

Decision criteria (must satisfy one):
1) Regional capacity SLO breach > 3 consecutive minutes AND sustained queue/backpressure causing customer errors.
2) Complete region network egress failure for the region's primary cloud provider AND cross-region fallback validated.
3) Legal instruction requiring immediate processing outside pinned region (only with Legal on-call involvement).
4) Active customer escalation where customer's business continuity is materially impacted and customer has signed fallback acceptance in contract/TOU.

Pre-override checklist (operator):
- Confirm decision criteria met. Capture metric snapshots (timestamped): regional CPU/GPU utilization, queue latency, error rate by tenant, prefix cache hit ratio.
- Confirm fallback target region (region code), instance type, and model compatibility (same model family/quantization).
- Ensure fallback storage encryption and KMS policy meet customer's contract obligations.
- Create a ticket (JIRA/INC) and start a short-running runbook entry. Use title format: "TEMP-OVRD <tenant> <src-region>-><dst-region> <hours>".
- Tag tenant: add runtime metadata label override:reason, override:initiated_by, override:expires_at (ISO8601).

Execution steps (safe procedure):
1) Prestage capacity: spin up dedicated nodes in fallback region and validate model loads with smoke prompts. Record node IDs and model hashes.
2) Create a canary route for 1–5% of tenant traffic for 10 minutes. Monitor for correctness and latency regressions.
3) If canary green: scale to agreed percentage (25% then 75%) with 5–10 minute observation windows.
4) If any correctness/regression detected: immediately revert canary to original region and escalate to engineering on-call.
5) When at target, mark the tenant as 'temporarily-routed' in the routing control plane with the metadata tags.

Telemetry and audit evidence (required for every override):
- Snapshot artifacts: pre-override metrics export (CSV), canary logs (first 10k requests), model hash and environment dump, operator approval emails/Slack thread link, ticket link.
- Telemetry keys to add: override.active=true, override.id=<ticket-id>, override.type=emergency|operational, override.ttl_hours=<n>.
- Ensure tracing includes original-client-region and routed-region fields for all affected requests.

Security & privacy review notes (quick):
- Do not fall back to regions that are contractually prohibited in the customer's account. System must refuse with an admin-visible error.
- For overrides triggered by legal process, Legal must author a one-line memo to attach to the ticket describing constraint. Redact PII when needed.
- KMS policy checks: ensure that key policies used in fallback region permit usage for tenant; if not, operator must coordinate with Key Mgmt team and obtain temporary key wrapping (avoid ad-hoc key creation).

TTL and automated rollback policy:
- Default TTL: 24 hours. Maximum TTL allowed via this playbook: 96 hours. Any request for TTL >96 hours requires formal product and legal paper trail and creation of a formal residency exception contract amendment.
- System action: at TTL expiration the control plane will auto-revert routing to pinned region. Operators must verify data sync and storage residency reconciliation post-revert.
- If operator-initiated early revert required, follow Revert checklist below.

Revert checklist (post-override):
- Verify all in-flight KV/prefix caches are flushed or reconciled to avoid cross-region cache poisoning.
- Run tenant-level data residency reconciliation job (id: residency-reconcile-v2) and export diff. Attach to ticket.
- Validate no write-after-read anomalies for affected tenants during override window.
- Update ticket with final evidence and close when legal/product sign-off obtained.

Common scenarios and worked examples:
- Scenario A: GCP europe-west1 network outage causes 40% increase in 5xx errors for EU-pinned tenant. Decision: Operational override to eu-west2 equivalent zone for 48 hours. Operators spun up nodes, ran canary at 2% then ramped. Evidence: pre/post latency CSV, canary logs. TTL set 48h.
- Scenario B: Lawful order requires immediate processing of a subset of logs in US for a regulatory checkpoint. Decision: Emergency override initiated after Legal on-call approval. TTL set 12h with Legal memo attached.
- Scenario C: Peak traffic during Black Friday causes dedicated pool exhaustion. If contractual fallback preapproved, execute operational override to dedicated-burst pool in same territory with TTL 6h.

Communication templates (Slack/email):
- Slack incident starter (to #residency-ops and legal-oncall):
  "TEMP OVERRIDE STARTED: tenant=<tenant-id> src=EU dst=US-east1 reason=region-outage approvers=@dkim @mnguyen ticket=JIRA-INC-7821 ttl=24h. Canary at 2% started. Monitoring: <grafana-link>. Post-hoc legal note pending."
- Customer-facing status blurb:
  "We are temporarily routing your workload to an alternate region to maintain availability while we resolve a regional outage. This change is temporary and will be reverted automatically within 24 hours. If you have contractual constraints, contact your account lead immediately."

Post-incident analysis (required template):
- Within 72 hours: Ops lead to publish a short postmortem covering root cause, why override was necessary, timeline of actions, telemetry exports, and recommendations to prevent recurrence (capacity, cross-region drain, pre-provisioning).
- Required attachments: ticket, logs, metrics CSV, legal memo (if any).

Tooling and automation improvements to propose (backlog):
- Auto-provisioning blue/green fallback capacity based on tenant risk score.
- One-click override in Console that assembles approval checkboxes, attaches artifacts, and tags telemetry automatically.
- Residency simulator that replays canary traffic under test to validate model hash compatibility ahead of incidents.

Open questions (for product/legal):
- Can we relax TTL to 7 days for high-complexity customers if they sign a temporary amendment? (Legal)
- Should we capture an explicit signed fallback consent checkbox in onboarding for SMBs? (Product)

Appendix: quick operator command snippets (internal CLI examples)
- mark-override --tenant=acme --from=eu-west1 --to=us-east1 --ttl=24h --ticket=JIRA-INC-7821 --reason="region-net-egress"
- rollback-override --tenant=acme --ticket=JIRA-INC-7821 --verify=true

Notes to reviewers:
- This playbook attempts to strike a balance between operational agility and auditability. Please review the authorization matrix and TTL caps carefully; legal input required on emergency path wording.
- If agreed, we will add a lightweight console flow to reduce operator manual steps and ensure telemetry keys are applied consistently.
